item.title: Chinese FM holds positive, constructive phone talks with Rubio on China-U.S. ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday held positive and constructive phone talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The two sides had an in-depth exchange of views on China-U.S. relations and the interaction between the two heads of state. During the talks, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that President Xi Jinping's visit to the United States in September was smooth and successful. The two heads of state agreed to enrich the connotation of a new vision of China-U.S. relations, providing clearer strategic guidance for exploring a right approach for the two countries to get along with each other, Wang said. The stable momentum of China-U.S. relations has not come easily and is the two major countries' rational choice based on their respective and common interests, Wang said. China, having maintained a stable and consistent policy towards the United States, is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the U.S. side, properly handle differences and sensitive issues, support each other in hosting the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit, and work to bring a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability into effect and deliver results, Wang said. ■

item.title: Belt and Road links deepen as freight trains run loaded both ways
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- China-Europe freight trains, a flagship project and signature brand of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), are now carrying full loads in both directions, with return trips slightly outnumbering outbound journeys, officials said here Wednesday. The service operated 18,661 trains and carried 1.865 million TEUs (Twenty-foot Equivalent Units) in the first 10 months of 2026, up 14.6 percent and 11.2 percent year on year, respectively, Liang Linchong, an official with the National Development and Reform Commission, told a press conference. Return trains totaled 9,360, against 9,301 outbound during the period, and the loaded container ratio has stayed at 100 percent for 50 consecutive months as of October, according to Liang. The land network behind the service has also widened. The trans-Caspian line now operates daily, and the northern, central and southern routes of China-Europe freight trains have maintained stable operations. Liang said the next phase for China-Europe freight trains would focus on four systems: efficient transport, safety governance, diversified routes and innovative development. Beyond rail, a canal opened this year gives China's southwestern inland regions a direct route to the sea, and air links now reach 159 cities in 66 BRI partner countries. China has signed Belt and Road cooperation documents with more than 150 countries and over 30 international organizations, Liang noted. Growing connectivity has been accompanied by growing trade. In the first three quarters, China's imports from partner countries grew 17.9 percent, 1.3 percentage points faster than its exports to them, according to official data. Trade with those partners has stayed above half of China's total goods trade since 2024. The corridor's financing arrangements have evolved alongside its traffic. Some 28 countries have endorsed Guiding Principles on Financing the Development of the Belt and Road, and China has promoted a debt sustainability framework for project analysis, Liang said. Trade rules have expanded as well. China has signed 19 free trade agreements with 25 Belt and Road partner countries and 92 bilateral investment treaties with partners, Song Lihong, an official with the Ministry of Commerce, told the briefing. In October, the United Nations Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents, initiated and spearheaded by China, saw 26 countries signing in the first round. The convention creates a negotiable cargo document applicable to all cross-border transport modes. Beyond large infrastructure projects, smaller ones with tangible benefits for local communities have also expanded. China's Juncao technology, which uses a type of grass to cultivate edible mushrooms and as livestock feed, is now used in more than 110 countries, and Luban Workshops, China's vocational education brand, operate 38 sites in 32 countries, among which 36 sites are in Belt and Road partner countries. It was noted at the briefing that the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) includes a dedicated chapter on high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. "We will continue to improve the 'four-in-one' connectivity network of land, sea, air and cyberspace," said Liang. ■

item.title: China's NEV share of new car sales continues to rise
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- New energy vehicles (NEVs) continued to gain ground in China's auto market in October, accounting for a larger share of new car sales, industry data showed on Wednesday. NEVs accounted for 64.3 percent of new car sales last month, up from 61.6 percent in September, while the cumulative share for the first 10 months climbed to 54.8 percent, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. In October, NEV output and sales reached about 2.02 million and 1.94 million units, respectively, both up by more than 13 percent year on year. ■

item.title: Russia, Ukraine resume talks after long hiatus, but breakthrough remains elusive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
* Zelensky said the discussions focused on security guarantees for Ukraine and mechanisms to ensure their long-term effectiveness, as well as steps toward de-escalation, adding that the main goal was to "truly bring peace closer." * Observers believe the trilateral talks could yield technical progress on less sensitive issues, such as humanitarian cooperation, localized ceasefires, safe corridors for grain exports and the establishment of a sustained dialogue mechanism. * Although the resumption of talks represents another attempt to resolve the conflict through diplomacy, the prospects for peace in the near term remain bleak. CAIRO/ABU DHABI, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- A new round of trilateral talks involving Russia, the United States and Ukraine entered its second day on Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The meeting marked the first trilateral talks among the three countries since February. Analysts say the talks have revived hopes for a diplomatic solution to the conflict, which has been dragging on for more than four years, and could pave the way for progress on practical issues, particularly humanitarian cooperation. However, they struck a more cautious note on the prospects for a comprehensive peace agreement, pointing to the lack of major breakthroughs in previous rounds of negotiations and the deep-rooted differences that continue to divide the two sides. RESUMPTION OF TALKS The delegations include several figures who have taken part in earlier rounds of negotiations, including Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and Ukrainian officials Rustem Umerov, head of the Foreign Intelligence Service, and Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Presidential Office. The first day of talks concluded after nearly four hours of discussions, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky describing the session as "constructive and quite substantive." In a post on social media platform X, Zelensky said the discussions focused on security guarantees for Ukraine and mechanisms to ensure their long-term effectiveness, as well as steps toward de-escalation, adding that the main goal was to "truly bring peace closer." At a press conference following the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also described the first day of talks in Abu Dhabi as "very productive." Despite the positive assessments, statements from Moscow and Kiev ahead of the talks suggested that the two sides had different expectations of what the latest round of negotiations should achieve. Russian Permanent Representative to the United Nations Vasily Nebenzya said Monday that Moscow opposes a "freeze" in the Ukraine conflict that would leave existing security threats unresolved and create conditions for renewed escalation. Ukraine, meanwhile, has called for an end to hostilities, reliable post-war security guarantees, economic recovery and development, as well as progress on humanitarian issues. The U.S. objective is "to bring Ukraine and Russia together to discuss directly their postwar security concerns, proposals, and potential solutions," Kushner said in a social media post before the talks. "We hope these discussions will identify areas of common ground, advance practical solutions, and build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations," he added. However, previous rounds of negotiations have shown that identifying common ground may be easier said than done. Following two days of talks in Geneva in February, during which Russian, U.S. and Ukrainian delegations held a total of eight hours of discussions but failed to reach agreement on key issues, direct talks among the three sides remained largely suspended for nine months. POSSIBLE PROGRESS, CORE DIVISIONS Observers believe the trilateral talks could yield technical progress on less sensitive issues, such as humanitarian cooperation, localized ceasefires, safe corridors for grain exports and the establishment of a sustained dialogue mechanism. Ahmed Al-Janabi, a UAE political analyst, said the importance of the talks lay not only in the possibility of reaching an agreement, but also in reopening negotiation channels to discuss the most complex issues, particularly security arrangements, stopping the escalation, humanitarian files and the future of the disputed areas. However, reconciliation still faces three major obstacles and constraints, according to the analysts. Firstly, fundamental differences remain difficult to bridge. Russia and Ukraine hold sharply opposing positions on fundamental issues such as territorial sovereignty and security guarantees, making it unlikely that their differences can be resolved in just one or two rounds of talks. Secondly, the battlefield situation continues to shape the pace of negotiations. Russia is currently maintaining its offensive along the frontline, while Ukraine continues to launch long-range strikes against Russian territory. Both sides seek to gain leverage in negotiations by gaining the upper hand on the battlefield. Thirdly, external factors, particularly those involving the United States and Europe, can also affect the talks. Political developments in both regions have added further uncertainty to the conflict and its diplomatic prospects. Amid all these challenges, territorial issues remain at the heart of the disagreements between Moscow and Kiev. "So far I see no grounds to say that territorial positions have noticeably converged. Kiev proposes a ceasefire to begin with. For Moscow, a ceasefire must become part of the terms of a final settlement," said Vadim Kozyulin, chief researcher at the Institute of Contemporary International Studies of the Russian Diplomatic Academy. "Territorial issues may simply not be on the agenda, but solutions can and must be sought," Kozyulin added. PEACE WITHOUT GUARANTEE Although the resumption of talks represents another attempt to resolve the conflict through diplomacy, the prospects for peace in the near term remain bleak. Ukraine is not expecting significant results from the first round of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, David Arakhamia, chairman of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction, a Ukrainian political party, told the media. He nevertheless acknowledged that resuming negotiations after a prolonged hiatus was an achievement in itself. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, meanwhile, made clear in his remarks on the negotiations that Moscow would not agree to calls for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine. Such statements from officials in both countries are consistent with analysts' assessments of the limited prospects for an early breakthrough. "This round of talks is not expected to yield decisive results. In the foreseeable short term, resolving this issue is a far-fetched goal," said Azza Hashem, managing director of the Cairo-based Al Habtoor Research Center. Despite some positive developments in recent times, "there is no indication that the underlying dynamics of the negotiations have changed," said John Herbst, senior director of the Atlantic Council's Eurasia Center. "Any realistic expectations for the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks should therefore be very modest," he said prior to the talks. Andrey Kortunov, a member of the Russian International Affairs Council, also expressed caution about the prospects for a comprehensive peace agreement. "It seems to me that it is still very far from a full-fledged peace. Although the negotiations have resumed, one cannot rule out the possibility of a new escalation in the very near future," Kortunov said. "I would like to hope that the conflict will eventually end, but no one can guarantee these timelines today," he added. (Video reporters: Wen Xinnian, Wang Hao, He Xinyuan, Wang Zecong; video editors: Liu Ruoshi, Zhang Yuhong.)■

item.title: China's Yangtze River Delta forges new quality productive forces through coordinated development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
SHANGHAI, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- In east China's Yangtze River Delta, a four-hour drive can take manufacturers through a network of suppliers capable of providing every component needed to build a new-energy vehicle. At one factory, a six-axis industrial robot can be produced every 12 minutes. These examples reflect a broad shift as the region turns its tightly clustered research and innovation hubs into advanced industrial capacity, making what China calls new quality productive forces the main engine of its growth. The Yangtze River Delta, comprising Shanghai and the provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui, now accounts for about one-quarter of China's GDP and nearly one-third of national R&D spending. According to a recent national assessment of regional science and technology innovation, Shanghai ranked first in comprehensive sci-tech innovation nationwide, with Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui also among the top performers. INNOVATION CLUSTERS This transformation is particularly visible in Shanghai's Zhangjiang Science City, where advanced industries are increasingly concentrated. At a lab in the Shanghai R&D center of XtalPi, an AI drug discovery company listed in Hong Kong, human researchers are largely absent. Weighing powders, controlling temperature during mixing, sampling, filtering and running post-processing analyzes are all handled by robotic workstations directed by AI, with large volumes of experimental data flowing continuously to back-end systems. "Zhangjiang offers a unique advantage in clustering innovation resources," said Wang Mingtai, XtalPi's senior vice president. "From overseas partners and major research institutes to upstream and downstream suppliers, connections can be established quickly here." By June 2026, the company had established partnerships with 17 of the world's top 20 pharmaceutical companies. Since the beginning of the year, more than six innovative drug programs involving its discovery technology had reported positive progress in clinical trials. Its autonomous research platform is also being applied in chemicals, new materials and new energy, alongside collaborations with leading universities and research institutes. The expanding network illustrates how Zhangjiang is bringing together scientific research, industrial partners and the development of new medicines and technologies, helping to move discoveries beyond the laboratory. Over the past five years, industrial output from firms above designated size in Zhangjiang has totaled 1.75 trillion yuan (about 260 billion U.S. dollars). In the first half of 2026, its three priority sectors -- integrated circuits, biomedicine and AI -- generated 82.28 billion yuan in output, up 14.8 percent from a year earlier. The area is now home to eight major global chip companies, 35 registered AI large models, and one in ten innovative drugs developed in China. Zhangjiang's experience shows how a concentration of research institutions, technology companies and industrial resources can accelerate innovation, driving new quality productive forces. The same approach is taking shape across the wider Yangtze River Delta, with its four provincial-level divisions complementing one another, especially in AI and the digital economy. COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS A recent digital development report describes this regional division of labor in simple terms: with Shanghai strengthening foundational research, Jiangsu focusing on manufacturing, Zhejiang excelling in application scenarios, and Anhui aggregating computing power. It allows companies to combine capabilities across the region and form a networked innovation system, rather than replicate them in one place. Jiangsu has made "AI Plus" a central driver of manufacturing upgrading. Under its action plan, the penetration rate of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents is expected to exceed 70 percent by 2027, with the AI industry surpassing 1 trillion yuan by 2030. In Suzhou, for example, efforts are underway to develop 150 industrial vertical large models, along with more than 200 high-quality industrial datasets, pushing AI applications from quality control and maintenance deeper into R&D and design. Zhejiang, meanwhile, is encouraging businesses to develop practical applications for AI, activating its intelligent economy. In 2025, the province's core AI industry revenue exceeded 710 billion yuan, growing by more than 20 percent. The capital city, Hangzhou, is positioning itself as a leading "AI city," deploying multimodal large models and embodied intelligence, while a major open-source model community and five 10,000-GPU computing clusters aim to lower the cost for small and medium-sized enterprises to adopt AI. Anhui is focusing on expanding its digital infrastructure and putting it to wider use. The province plans to build 14,000 new 5G base stations and 4,000 5G-A base stations in 2026, with intelligent computing capacity exceeding 65,000 petaflops. A special fund for data-element reform in the province will support AI scenario projects with up to 10 million yuan each, accelerating deployment in manufacturing, public services and healthcare. CROSS-REGIONAL LINKS Cooperation across the Yangtze River Delta extends beyond AI and the digital economy. It also shows how innovation capacity generated in one city can be rapidly converted into industrial output in another. Suzhou, for example, has 50 enterprises in the supply chain for China's C919 passenger aircraft assembled in Shanghai, and about 180 auto-parts manufacturers have become tier-one suppliers for Shanghai-based SAIC Volkswagen and Tesla. Meanwhile, scientific instruments at Shanghai's universities and research institutes can be booked online by Suzhou enterprises for remote testing and cross-regional settlement. As of October 2026, the Yangtze River Delta region had shared 75,000 sets of large-scale scientific instruments, with sci-tech innovation vouchers covering about 820 million yuan in services. These links make integration tangible: firms can access specialized suppliers and costly scientific equipment across administrative boundaries, lowering duplication and making better use of existing resources. Luo Dajin, director of the Shanghai municipal science and technology commission, said Shanghai would build on its strengths as an international economic, financial, trade, shipping and sci-tech innovation hub, and work with Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui to build a sci-tech innovation corridor and other joint innovation zones across the region. Recent data suggest the shift is gaining momentum. In the first three quarters of 2026, high-tech manufacturing output grew 15.1 percent in Jiangsu, 16 percent in Zhejiang and 50.3 percent in Anhui, while Shanghai's three priority industries expanded by 17.1 percent. The region's division of labor has moved beyond the old linear pattern of industrial relocation from Shanghai, Jiangsu and Zhejiang to Anhui, and is now shaped by functional and structural complementarity, said Zeng Gang, director of the Institute of Urban Development, East China Normal University. "New quality productive forces have become the main engine of industrial growth in the Yangtze River Delta," he said. ■

item.title: NEVs gain further ground in China's auto market, nearing two-thirds of new vehicle sales
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's shift toward new energy vehicles (NEVs) gathered pace in October, with NEVs making up nearly two out of every three new vehicles sold, industry data showed Wednesday. NEVs accounted for 64.3 percent of new car sales last month, up from 61.6 percent in September, while the cumulative share for the first 10 months climbed to 54.8 percent, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM). Exports of NEVs surged about 140 percent year on year to 606,000 units in October, accounting for more than half of China's auto exports for a fifth consecutive month. NEVs, which include battery electric, plug-in hybrid and fuel-cell vehicles, recorded output and sales of about 2.02 million and 1.94 million units, respectively, in October, both up more than 13 percent year on year. Among NEV passenger cars, models priced between 100,000 yuan (about 14,883 U.S. dollars) and 150,000 yuan formed the largest sales bracket in the January-October period. Sales in this price range increased 14.5 percent year on year to almost 3.14 million units, CAAM data showed. The shift toward new energy also extended to commercial vehicles, including trucks and buses. NEVs accounted for 51.9 percent of domestic commercial vehicle sales in October, with domestic sales of such vehicles rising 36 percent year on year to 112,000 units. On the export side, China's total vehicle exports rose 60.2 percent year on year to nearly 1.07 million units in October, remaining above the 1-million mark for a fifth consecutive month. In the first 10 months, NEV exports increased 130 percent to 4.61 million units, already exceeding the 2.615 million shipped overseas in the whole of 2025. Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the China Passenger Car Association, told China Securities Journal on Tuesday that global electrification, high oil prices, expanding markets in developing economies and the growing competitiveness of Chinese vehicles were supporting export growth. He also highlighted China's comprehensive NEV supply chain, rapid product development and plug-in hybrid models suited to different driving needs. The export surge comes as China prepares to lower tax rebates for NEVs. The Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration announced in October that the value-added tax export rebate rate for these vehicles will fall from 13 percent to 9 percent on April 1, 2027. While the lower rebate would raise export costs in the short term, particularly for models with thin profit margins, Cui said in a separate article that the industry's export growth was underpinned by its supply chains and technological capabilities rather than tax incentives. He said the adjustment would encourage automakers to move away from disorderly low-price competition, develop higher-value products and deepen local operations overseas, helping shift their global expansion from volume growth toward higher-quality development. ■

item.title: PLA Air Force marks 77th anniversary amid modernization drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force marked its 77th founding anniversary on Wednesday, highlighting its journey from a modest beginning to a modernizing force with a structure geared toward future operational needs. In an anniversary video, the Air Force, founded on Nov. 11, 1949, showcased training exercises involving fighter jets, bombers, early warning aircraft, transport planes, helicopters and drones, as well as ground-based air defense missile units, radar units and airborne troops. The video, released Wednesday on the service's official social media accounts, also highlighted the Air Force's participation in disaster relief and international exchanges, drawing a wave of congratulatory messages. Anniversary celebrations had begun earlier this month, with events held in different parts of the country. On Monday morning, eight flight instructors from the Aviation University of the Air Force in Changchun, capital of northeast China's Jilin Province, took to the skies in jet trainers for an aerial display. That evening, 3,000 drones lit up the sky in a light show depicting the Air Force's evolution, from horse-towed propeller-driven trainer aircraft, to advanced aircraft such as J-20 stealth fighter and Y-20 transport plane. On Nov. 6, six J-10 jets from the PLA Air Force's Bayi (August 1) Aerobatic Team flew over the Great Wall in north China's Tianjin Municipality as part of the celebrations. The team derives its name from the founding anniversary of the PLA. "The Great Wall was once a barrier against invaders," said Zha Xiufeng, one of the pilots. "Today, we pilots serve as an 'airborne Great Wall,' safeguarding the peace and security of countless families." The PLA Air Force started with a small fleet of outdated aircraft. During the founding ceremony of the People's Republic of China on Oct. 1, 1949, only 17 aircraft were available for parade. In the following years, the Air Force shot down or damaged more than 3,800 enemy aircraft, according to official figures. More than 1,800 Air Force personnel have given their lives in combat operations, scientific research tasks, and dedication to the interests of the people. The PLA Air Force's three-step development roadmap, issued in 2018, set targets to build a strategic air force by 2020, basically establish a modernized strategic air force by 2035, and become a world-class air force by the middle of the century. The 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, scheduled to run from Dec. 7 to 13 in Zhuhai, will offer the world a glimpse of the PLA Air Force's latest developments. The Air Force said multiple types of its main combat equipment would make their debut at the show. Equipment for aerial reconnaissance, early warning, air defense, support, airborne operations, unmanned applications and intelligent systems, as well as munitions, will also be displayed at the exhibition. "Bringing more domestically developed new-generation aircraft closer to the public and taking Air Force stories into households across the country are commitments we will continue to uphold," said Gao Xiang, a senior Air Force official. As the PLA Air Force has developed, its international engagement has also expanded. In 2026, the Bayi Aerobatic Team performed at the 10th Singapore Airshow, while a range of aircraft, including fighters, tankers, special-purpose aircraft and helicopters, took part in the China-Egypt "Eagles of Civilization 2026" joint air force training as an integrated force. Moreover, Chinese and Russian air forces conducted a joint strategic patrol over the western Pacific and other airspace, demonstrating their resolve and capability to uphold regional peace and stability. Chinese and Belarusian airborne troops also held urban counterterrorism exercises in central China. "We will continue to engage with our counterparts around the world, build mutual trust through interaction, deepen cooperation through exchanges, and work together to safeguard the shared airspace of humanity," Gao said. ■

item.title: Book of Xi's discourses on poverty reduction, alleviation published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A compilation of discourses by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on poverty reduction and alleviation has been published by the Central Party Literature Press and released nationwide. Compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the book brings together 55 important articles by Xi on poverty reduction and alleviation. Some of these works are made public for the first time. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core has placed poverty alleviation high on its governance agenda and regarded it as the bottom line task in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. China has won a complete victory in the fight against poverty and accomplished the arduous task of eliminating absolute poverty, creating a miracle in the human history of poverty reduction. In the process, the country has blazed a poverty reduction path and formed an anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics. Xi's discourses on poverty reduction and alleviation represent an important theoretical achievement in China's poverty alleviation efforts and the latest achievement in adapting Marxist anti-poverty theory to the Chinese context. These discourses provide important guidance for consolidating and expanding the achievements in poverty alleviation and advancing rural revitalization across the board, promoting modernization that delivers common prosperity for all, and building a better world free from poverty and featuring shared prosperity. ■
